verdict.rationale: Exa documents a web search API that takes natural-language queries and returns ranked, relevance-sized results from its own index, including a deep-reasoning search mode (exa-docs-60, exa-docs-22, exa-docs-36, exa-docs-18). That is the core of meaning-based search, though the pack never explicitly describes embedding/neural retrieval. Hands-on reports are mixed: one user was impressed and a founder said SERPs are the wrong interface for LLMs (exa-comm-1, exa-comm-8), but another estimated only about 30/70 accuracy on a repo search (exa-comm-2), and the 2022 Metaphor launch returned off-target results (exa-comm-10, exa-comm-11). These show quality limits rather than contradicting the capability, so the verdict is partial, not disputed. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of semantic/neural retrieval, evidence of results that keyword engines miss, and consistent independent relevance corroboration.
